title: The morning sheet
blurb: Every location on one page before opening, built from the point of sale and from the supplier invoices it cannot see.
replaces: Opening three portals and rebuilding yesterday by hand
point: A 2% price drift nobody caught, on $70k of monthly purchasing, is roughly $1,400 a month

title: Avo
blurb: You say it once. It reaches the website, Instagram and Google in three different registers, and the agent checks the page before it tells you it is done.
replaces: Writing one announcement four times, then not being sure the fourth went out
point: Every channel is verified against the live page, so the one that silently did not publish is caught the same morning

title: The invoice reader
blurb: Drop in one supplier invoice, PDF or photo. Your own lines come back with a price per kilogram beside each, and anything it cannot price honestly is set aside with the reason. Nothing is kept.
replaces: A calculator, the invoice, and guessing what is inside a 4/5 LB case
time: about 10 minutes per invoice, done properly
point: Two cases at the same price can hide a 20% difference per kilogram, and only the division shows it

title: Where the delivery money went
blurb: DoorDash, Uber Eats and SkipTheDishes payout statements checked against the POS and the bank, order by order. Commission kept on refunded orders, payouts that never landed, deposits that came in short.
replaces: Ticking app payouts against the bank only when the month looks off
time: about 2 hours a month for a two-site group, if anyone does it
point: At $40,000 a month through the apps, a one percent gap between statement and bank is $400 a month

title: Price sync
blurb: One price change across the till, the website and three delivery apps. Every channel checked against your own markup rule, what each sale really leaves, an approval step, and a second look after the send that catches the app which said yes and changed nothing.
replaces: The same price edit in five admin screens, and hoping all five took
time: about 2 hours per price round, plus the drift nobody sees
point: Three weeks of app prices lagging a 4% increase, on $40,000 a month through the apps, is about $1,200

title: Tips, ready for payroll
blurb: A week of tips across four rooms. The missed clock-out and the owner behind the bar are decided by a person, not guessed by a formula. Split to the cent by written rules, signed off per room, and every member of staff gets their own working on their phone.
replaces: A manager, a spreadsheet and two hours per room every pay period
time: about 2 hours per room per pay period
point: At 4 rooms, 2 hours each, 26 pay periods and $35 an hour, that is about $7,300 a year of manager time, before the disputes
